mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter credit conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp over the next month
failure_condition: In a rising FEDFUNDS regime with no other macro changes, 20-day SPX forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate prolonged easing and increased equity valuation multiples.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the three-month decline, SPX 20-day forward returns are not higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (household spending) exceeds the prior month's value by at least 2% and UNRATE falls below 4%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive as consumer demand recovers and labor market slack increases.
candidate_trigger: HOUST up ≥2% AND UNRATE down < 4% from previous month
regime_hint: Recovery in consumer demand with easing labor market
failure_condition: In such trigger events, 20-day SPX forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 10,000 over the prior month coincides with a negative S&P 5-day forward return as the labor market becomes over-supplied and wage growth softens equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 over prior month
failure_condition: In such events, 5-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls for two consecutive months below its 12-month moving average, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative as weak supply signals a risk-off environment.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months below 12-mo MA
failure_condition: In this regime, 20-day SPX forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST by at least 3% in the prior quarter are associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as strong demand supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 up ≥3% AND HOUST up ≥3% in prior quarter
failure_condition: Over 60 days following the quarter, SPX 20-day forward returns are not higher than the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to inflation expectations eroding equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% MoM for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In such a regime, 20-day SPX forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent labor market tightness and higher wage growth compressing earnings growth.
failure_condition: In this regime, 60-day SPX forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (p > 0.05).
